content:
**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected part**: A single sugarcane leaf, viewed in close-up
- **Color**: Pronounced bright yellow coloration concentrated along the midrib (central vein), with the surrounding lamina tissue appearing pale cream/yellow
- **Pattern**: The yellowing radiates outward from the midrib — no discrete spots, no mosaic patterning, no streaks with alternating green/yellow bands, no necrotic/brown lesions
- **Texture**: Smooth, no distortion or rot visible

**Differential reasoning:**

| Class | Key feature | Match? |
|---|---|---|
| Brown_Spot | Brown necrotic spots | No |
| Grassy_Shoot | Multiple thin grassy proliferations | No |
| Leaf_Scald | Scalded water-soaked lesions with yellow halo | No |
| Pokkah_Boeng | Twisted/distorted young leaves with chlorosis | No |
| Sett_Rot | Rot of sett/cutting | No |
| Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv | Distinct streaks of alternating yellow/green | No |
| Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus | Mosaic of light/dark green | No |
| **Yellow_Leaf** | **Midrib yellowing, extending outward across lamina** | **Yes** |
| Yellow_Spot | Discrete yellow spots | No |

The bright, continuous yellow band along the midrib that extends into the surrounding leaf tissue is the hallmark of **Yellow Leaf Syndrome** (caused by Sugarcane yellow leaf virus), which specifically causes midrib yellowing on the abaxial surface as the primary and most diagnostic symptom.
